clue.text: He's upset 16-he wants payment

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the referenced answer are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: 16 refers to the answer at 16 Down, a manager of a company

explanation.surface: Someone is upset and is demanding to be paid what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the letters of DIRECTOR, the answer at 16 Down, into a new word; 'He's' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender is owed money and so is the person seeking to be paid back.

clue.text: A once-respected figure is repeatedly put down

indicators.note: repeatedly put down means the little word is written out on the page twice in a row

explanation.surface: A formerly admired person keeps being belittled.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the clue word 'is' down twice. The figure is the Egyptian goddess, revered in ancient times and no longer worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mother goddess was venerated in antiquity, a deity once honoured and now only a figure of history.

clue.text: The rascally fellow's broken cover, that's clear

indicators.note: broken means the rascal has broken into the cover, sitting inside it

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box
an imp is a mischievous rascal of a child

explanation.surface: A villain's disguise has slipped, so now everything is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' tells us IMP has broken into LID, giving L-IMP-ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water or prose is transparent and easy to see through or understand.

clue.text: This neat solution is in doubt

indicators.note: solution here is a dissolving or working out, so the letters of the two words are mixed afresh

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a tidy answer is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' acts on the eight letters of 'This neat', rearranging them; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wavering and uncertain holds back, unsure what to do.

clue.text: Allowance obtained through an embassy

parts.note: per means by way of or through, as in 'per post'
a diplomatic mission is an embassy abroad

explanation.surface: A visa or entitlement is secured via a foreign diplomatic office.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allowed to do something is having leave or consent granted.

clue.text: On average letters for the queen appear less charitable

parts.note: the mean is the average, so on average is the mean
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Statistically, mail addressed to the monarch looks less generous.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean is stingy or unkind, and the comparative form describes someone even stingier.

clue.text: Fly without a break, causing stress

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the break sits within the other piece

parts.note: to wing is to fly
a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: Flying non-stop is a strain on the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so the fly piece goes around the break. 'Without a break' wants to mean non-stop, which is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wresting means wrenching or straining something by force, twisting it under tension.

clue.text: Go round inflicting injury

parts.note: a ring is something round, a circle

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a circuit while hurting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Goring is wounding with horns or tusks, as a bull or boar does.

clue.text: A group of players quite possibly cross one

explanation.surface: A team might be crossing one particular line.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross is X and one is I, together XI, the Roman numeral for the number of players in a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team fields this many players; also the Roman numeral X followed by I spells the number.

clue.text: The likelihood of scraps

explanation.surface: A question about how probable leftovers are.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is from 'odds and ends', bits and pieces; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting chances express probability, and miscellaneous leftovers are bits and pieces.

clue.text: Part male in composition-it's convention

indicators.note: composition means the letters are being composed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of music partly written by a man is called conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges the ten letters of 'Part male in'; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A national assembly or legislature is a formal convention of representatives.

clue.text: Dull-witted goody-goody taken in by boss

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: a stud is a raised boss or knob on a surface
pi is crossword shorthand for pious, a goody-goody

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious, slow employee is fooled by their manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' here is not a manager but a raised knob or stud; PI (pious) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, dim-brained person is foolish and dense.

clue.text: Coppers taking certain steps in an outbreak

indicators.note: taking means the coins hold the steps inside them

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pennies, so pence
a stile is a set of steps over a fence

explanation.surface: Police officers climb certain steps during a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' are not police but copper coins, PENCE; a STILE is the steps for crossing a field fence, common in British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague or epidemic disease sweeping through a population is a deadly outbreak.

clue.text: Antediluvian enterprise

parts.note: antediluvian usually means very old-fashioned, but literally it means before the Flood, so the venture is the biblical boat-building project

explanation.surface: An outdated business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel built before the biblical Flood was the great project of the pre-Flood era.

clue.text: Stay on the subject of 9

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
9 Across is a team of players, and a team is a side

explanation.surface: Remain on the topic of a cross-referenced clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 9 Across is a team, so stands for SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To live or dwell somewhere is to stay there.

clue.text: The manager of 1 being awkward

indicators.note: being awkward means the letters are put into a clumsy new order

parts.note: 1 refers to 1 Down, someone who is owed money

explanation.surface: A boss reacts to someone being difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being awkward' rearranges CREDITOR, the answer at 1 Down; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A company head or someone running a film is in charge, a boss.

clue.text: Institute industrial action and create an impression

explanation.surface: Walk out on strike and make your mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkout is industrial action, and to stamp a coin or medal is to make an impression.

clue.text: The Spanish needle one bearing a different way

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
to sew is to work with a needle
I is the Roman numeral one
SE, south-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A Spanish needle points somewhere unexpected.
explanation.definitionFit: Means otherwise or in another manner.

clue.text: Fail in examinations, and so work as a farm-hand

explanation.surface: A student flunks and goes off to till the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to fail an exam is to be ploughed; 'and so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British university slang for failing a candidate, and the farm job of turning soil with a blade.

clue.text: Military men backing tribal split dealing with dispute

indicators.note: backing means read backwards, going in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, soldiers

indicators.note: split means the word tribal is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers supporting a divided tribe are caught up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the Royal Artillery round, and 'split' rearranges the letters of 'tribal'. RA is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to arbitration, the settling of disagreements by a neutral party.

clue.text: Celebrity taking note about English place

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A famous person writes a memo about somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'about' are link words here.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity in the sense of fame or renown, a good name.

clue.text: Expatriate in a turban is Hindu

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An emigrant wearing a turban is a Hindu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expatriate' is a verb here, to send out of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone from their country is to send them away for good.

clue.text: Cricketer well-known as a crime-fighter

explanation.surface: A cricket player also famous as a vigilante.
explanation.walkthrough: A bat man wields the bat in cricket; the crime-fighter is the caped comic-book hero. 'well-known as a' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman holds the bat in cricket, and a caped comic hero fights crime in Gotham.

clue.text: Topping bread for the aristocracy!

parts.note: upper is top, the higher layer
the crust is the outer part of bread

explanation.surface: A slice of fine bread fit for nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest social class, the elite at the top like the crust on a loaf.

clue.text: Many have cut down

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Lots of people have been felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass or hay that has been cut is scythed down.

clue.text: Maiden head-ancient town

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word maiden

parts.note: old means ancient

explanation.surface: Maidenhead is an old English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town in Berkshire, a red herring; the answer is the Welsh market town.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in north-east Wales, county town of Flintshire.

clue.text: Chisels back onto firm plaster

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round, read from right to left

parts.note: chisels cuts, as a sculptor does
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Carving tools are rested against a solid wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CUTS to STUC; 'onto' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine plaster or render used for coating walls and mouldings.

clue.text: Lacking capital, and that's no life!

definitions.text: Lacking capital, and that's no life!

parts.words: Lacking capital, and that's no life!
parts.note: capital is the head, so lacking capital means without a head, a state that is certainly no life

explanation.surface: Being broke is a miserable existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' wants to be money; here it is the head on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Without the topmost body part, as in beheaded, and so no longer alive.
